intro.heading: Skyline Cruises Offers Incredible Nautical Weddings
paragraphs: Have you always dreamed of a wedding at sea and being married by a ship captain? Forget what you may have seen in an old “Love Boat” rerun. It’s rarer than you think.
“It’s a myth that a captain can marry a person on a cruise ship,” Captain Arnold said in an interview that appears on his website. Unless he’s ordained or a member of the clergy.

Fortunately, Captain Arnold is an ordained chaplain. He’s also been a Coast Guard licensed captain for more than 40 years. In fact, he’s the only captain who’s also registered as an ordained chaplain with the City Clerk’s office in New York City.
So how did Captain Arnold start to perform weddings? He started doing it aboard private yachts in Florida. He says “it kind of gave me a bit of a niche” when he returned to New York.

extraTextSections.heading: Captain Arnold’s Ceremony of Love
paragraphs: Captain Arnold certainly looks impressive in his dress uniform with gold stripes when he performs wedding ceremonies on the top level all weather rooftop deck, known as the “Skylight Deck” on the Skyline Princess. But it’s his “ceremony of love” that couples will remember forever.
“It deals mostly with love, what marriage is about,” he says. “I don’t use any negative words, I don’t say ‘In sickness and in health,’ or say, ”until death do you part.’ ”

hero.h1: The World’s Fair Marina – Flushing, Queens, NY

paragraphs: The World’s Fair Marina is a public marina located at the northern edge of Flushing Meadows-Corona. Conveniently located right off the Grand Central Parkway, this public marina is just north of Citi-Field, home to the MLB’s New York Metropolitans, as well as the USTA National Tennis Center, home of the U.S. Open.

Originally a boat basin built in 1939 for the World’s Fair, Robert Moses expanded the construction of the marina for the 1964 New York World’s Fair to help accommodate over 800 boats. Since 1999, the NYC Department of Parks & Recreation has operated the World’s Fair Marina.

The marina offers many different activities including power boating, kayaking, canoeing, ferries, as well as party boats and even larger yachts such as the Skyline Princess. The World’s Fair Marina location offers public dinner cruises as well as public brunch cruises and lunch cruises. If you are looking for a unique party idea, you can also launch a party boat charter or holiday cruise from this location and enjoy the finest catering on the open seas!

Chelsea Piers is located on the West Side of Manhattan in Chelsea, New York City. The series of piers is west of the West Side Highway and east of the Hudson River.

Originally, Chelsea Piers referred to the luxury liner berths on Manhattan’s west side from 1910 to the 1930s. Famous ships such as the Lusitania docked there. In the mid-1980s, the piers were in danger of being destroyed when there were plans to rebuild the West Side Highway. Once these plans fell through, The Department of Transportation held an auction in 1992 for the property. Roland W. Betts won the auction and transformed the dilapidated piers into its current incarnation.

There are several activities and complexes that now inhabit Chelsea Piers; the Golf Club, the Sports Center health club, Sky Rink, the Field House, MarineMax Maritime Center, Bowlmor, the Pier Sixty and Lighthouse event centers and not to mention Skyline Princess Cruises. If you are looking for an NYC yacht charter for a private dinner cruise, Skyline Princess Cruises can launch from Chelsea Piers. paragraphs: Overlooking Hempstead Bay, the Glen Cove Ferry Terminal is located on the north side of the channel, right off Garvies Point.

The Glen Cove Ferry Terminal, nestled on the picturesque shores of Long Island’s North Shore, serves as a vital link connecting Glen Cove to Manhattan. The surrounding area boasts a blend of maritime charm and modern amenities, with waterfront parks, dining establishments, and recreational opportunities all within easy reach. The harbor is a hub of activity, featuring pleasure boats, fishing vessels, and the occasional visiting yacht, creating a lively atmosphere that reflects the area’s deep connection to the water.
A fun fact: Glen Cove was once known as “Musketa Cove” by the Matinecock Native Americans, and later by early English settlers, before officially becoming Glen Cove in 1834.

Historically, Glen Cove played a significant role in the region’s industrial and social development. During the Gilded Age, it became a favored summer retreat for wealthy industrialists, resulting in the construction of grand mansions that still dot the landscape. The Webb Institute, a prestigious naval architecture and marine engineering college, is a testament to the area’s maritime heritage. Today, Glen Cove maintains a vibrant community, with a bustling downtown area featuring diverse shops, restaurants, and cultural attractions. The local area surrounding the ferry terminal offers a blend of suburban tranquility and urban accessibility, making it an attractive destination for both residents and visitors seeking a taste of Long Island’s coastal charm.

Glen Cove’s harbor provides an excellent starting point for Skyline Cruises’ Long Island Lighthouse and Gold Coast tours. The proximity to iconic lighthouses and opulent Gold Coast mansions allows for a captivating journey through maritime history and Gilded Age grandeur. The ease of navigating from Glen Cove into the Long Island Sound ensures a smooth and enjoyable cruise, making it a prime location for these scenic excursions.
